description: Team of computer science students interested in innovation.
summary:
OUTPOST ZERO is a browser-based space survival game where players take charge of a small astronaut outpost. Their task is to manage limited power and keep important systems running while looking after the crew. As the mission progresses, players must think carefully about how they use their resources and deal with the challenges of living on the Moon. The game introduces young players to some of the real difficulties involved in planning a space mission.
Play the game here: https://aleetaminnu.github.io/junior-astronaut-outpost-zero/
details:
Play the game here: https://aleetaminnu.github.io/junior-astronaut-outpost-zero/

Github repository: https://github.com/Aleetaminnu/junior-astronaut-outpost-zero

​

The game begins with the player taking charge of an outpost on the Moon. The mission is divided into days, and the player has a limited amount of power to work with. They must keep track of important resources such as air, food and radiation shielding, while also making sure that the crew remains healthy.

You need to scroll down the how to play page to find 'Start mission' button.

*Some cool features:* Tapping the buildings on the small overview map also takes you there. You can move to a tapped location during gameplay even if it is not a building.


The Mission Control screen displays the current stage, day and resource levels. This helps players understand the condition of their outpost before deciding what to do next. The player can interact with the outpost and advance the mission using the END DAY button.

Space weather is also included in the game. The page checks NASA's DONKI database for space-weather information when it is available. If the data cannot be reached, the game can use saved events instead. This helps introduce players to the effects that space weather can have on space missions.

The resource values have been simplified for gameplay. They are not meant to be exact measurements of a real Moon mission, but they help demonstrate why power, life support and radiation protection are important.

We wanted the game to be simple enough for young players to understand while still giving them a small idea of the challenges astronauts and mission planners face.
